transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date/Time: Tue Sep 29 2026 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (CTO - Tidewave), Mark Reynolds (Head of MLOps), Priya Singh (Infrastructure), Samir Gupta (Product)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
- Tidewave is approaching renewal; they're interested in expanding dedicated capacity and adding EU region.
- Main asks: deterministic latency at peak (99th), predictable unit cost, SOC2/network docs for legal.
- Redwood to run a 1-week dedicated benchmark and provide updated pricing and contract draft.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you carving time today. this is Maya from Redwood Inference, i'm the account exec on this deal.
[00:12] Asha Patel: hey Maya, thanks. i think we have about 45 minutes, wanted to focus on capacity numbers and the EU region ask.
[00:20] Luis Ortega: hi all, Luis here, i'll be running the bench and technical bits; sorry for the slight echo i got on my side.
[00:28] Mark Reynolds: cool. quick context, we run two main clusters, east-us primaries, spike traffic eom, currently at ~120 qps across our main endpoints, 99th latency we see ~480ms on the hosted endpoints during spikes.
[00:45] Maya Chen: got it. and your current contract is up in late october right? renewal window?
[00:52] Priya Singh: yeah, october 28th is renewal date, we'd like to lock something in sooner, especially if we're adding an EU region.
[01:03] Maya Chen: ok, makes sense. prelim questions - is data residency required in EU for PII workloads or just lower latency?
[01:12] Asha Patel: it's primarily latency for user-facing features, but a subset of customers require EU residency, so ideally we have the option for regionally isolated endpoints.
[01:22] Samir Gupta: and also want predictable budget - if cost spikes by 2-3x at eom we get complaints from finance.
[01:29] Luis Ortega: yeah so capacity options - we can do additional dedicated pools in eu-west, or we can route to hosted with reserved burst. dedicated gives you isolation and stable throughput; hosted is cheaper but less predictable at 99th under peak.
[01:44] Mark Reynolds: can you walk through the latency guarantees on dedicated? last time we saw 'Redwood Dedicate' - uh, 'Redwood Dedicated' - we had some warmup jitter.
[01:56] Luis Ortega: totally. for dedicated capacity we provision pinned GPU nodes, we guarantee baseline throughput and we set autoscale policies. typical 99th for similar profiles is sub-200ms for gen endpoints with KV cache cold start mitigations. there is still warmup on very long sequences but the delta's usually 30-80ms.
[02:18] Priya Singh: the warmup you're describing, is that per-model or per-instance? we saw weird KV cache invalidations last quarter.
[02:27] Luis Ortega: it's mostly cache warmup per instance and per model shard; we do prefix caching and continuous batch priority, but rare invalidations happen if model variants change. we'll include more detail in the runbook.
[02:38] Asha Patel: ok. question on pricing - what are the increments for dedicated? we have variable QPS across endpoints, some endpoints are low QPS but high latency sensitivity.
[02:48] Maya Chen: we do tiered capacity blocks - you can reserve X vGPU units for a baseline and then add burst capacity. i'll send the exact tiers in the quote. we can also add per-endpoint routing to favor lower-latency pools.
[03:03] Mark Reynolds: what's the delta if we add EU region at the same committed capacity? like is there a cross-region surcharge?
[03:09] Maya Chen: there's a regional add-on fee to cover infra costs and cross-region replication where needed. i'll include a regional price table.
[03:16] Samir Gupta: are there minimum terms for Dedicated? we prefer 12 months but want flexibility to ramp.
[03:22] Maya Chen: standard is 12-month commits for dedicated with quarterly review; we can do tiered ramps in the contract so you can step up mirrors. legal can draft a ramp schedule.
[03:31] Priya Singh: on security we need SOC 2, iso docs and network diagrams for our legal. also SSO/SAML and KMS with customer-managed keys.
[03:40] Luis Ortega: yep we have SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 artifacts; private deployments support bring-your-own KMS/HSM in our Private offering. for Dedicated in VPC peering we support CMK integrations and audit logs. i'll attach the network diagram.
[03:55] Asha Patel: can you clarify the differences between Redwood Private and Dedicated? we've been discussing both internally.
[04:02] Luis Ortega: sure - Dedicated is managed capacity in our infra, isolated pools per customer with peering options. Private is customer-managed control plane, either VPC or on-prem, full isolation and control for compliance. Private has higher ops overhead and longer lead time.
[04:19] Mark Reynolds: lead time for Private? months?
[04:22] Luis Ortega: typically 6-10 weeks depending on integrations and air-gap needs. Dedicated pockets can be provisioned in 2-3 weeks.
[04:30] Priya Singh: that's significant. for the immediate renewal we probably want dedicated + EU region and evaluate Private for next year.
[04:38] Maya Chen: understood. sounds like a plan - we'll propose a 12-month dedicated commit with a ramp schedule and an option to pursue Private next year.
[04:47] Asha Patel: another question - we'd like a hard SLA for uptime and latency credits. what do you typically offer?
[04:54] Maya Chen: we offer SLA-backed uptime targets and latency SLOs for Dedicated with credits tied to measurable breaches. i'll include the SLA language in the draft.
[05:04] Mark Reynolds: ok good. on the benchmarks, can we run our real traffic replay or do we need synthetic?
[05:11] Luis Ortega: replay is best - we can ingest traces (PII redacted) or we can run a recorded trace in our benchmark harness. if you can share a 24h trace sample we can reproduce spikes.
[05:21] Priya Singh: we can provide a trace with headers removed, yes. due to residency some traces for EU users will need separate handling.
[05:29] Samir Gupta: on logs - retention and access controls? finance/legal want proof that logs are retained x days and accessible via API or S3 bucket.
[05:38] Luis Ortega: we have configurable retention for audit logs and can ship to your S3 or SIEM; default is 90 days, extended retention is an add-on.
[05:47] Asha Patel: competitors - we've had talks with Anthropic and ApexInfer; their pricing looks aggressive but we like Redwood's runtime performance.
[05:57] Maya Chen: appreciate the context. we can run a comp benchmark and show unit economics.
[06:03] Mark Reynolds: one nit - last time we saw a nightly batch job that spiked costs due to naive batching; is there a way to isolate low-cost batch workloads from the latency-sensitive ones?
[06:14] Luis Ortega: yep, route batch jobs to cheaper quantized model variants and separate pools; Redwood Optimize recommendations can help configure batching thresholds and quant profiles.
[06:25] Asha Patel: perfect. any blockers on your side to give us pricing by next week?
[06:30] Maya Chen: no blockers. i'll put together the dedicated + eu add-on quote and the ramp language.
[06:36] Priya Singh: can we also get a sample MSA with the ramp annex? legal needs to start review.
[06:41] Maya Chen: yes, i'll loop in legal and send draft MSA.
[06:44] Samir Gupta: timeline - we need the pricing and MSA before october 5 to align finance approval.
[06:49] Maya Chen: noted, target october 1 for quote and october 2 for MSA draft.
[06:54] Luis Ortega: for the benchmark i'll need 24h traffic trace and a spec of sequences and max tokens. can you drop that to me?
[07:02] Mark Reynolds: will do, i'll export traces and remove headers today.
[07:06] Priya Singh: one more security note - we require customer-managed KMS for any EU residency data.
[07:13] Luis Ortega: we support CMK for Dedicated + Private, we'll add the KMS integration steps in the runbook.
[07:20] Asha Patel: great. anything else?
[07:23] Maya Chen: quick recap of next steps - i'll send pricing + MSA, Luis will run benchmark once traces arrive, Priya to share SLA and regional requirements. we'll reconvene after benchmark results.
[07:34] Samir Gupta: works for me. thanks all.
[07:36] Mark Reynolds: thanks.
[07:38] Priya Singh: thanks.
[07:40] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, talk soon. bye.

End of transcript.

References/Artifacts mentioned:
